questions.explanation: Juran's definition focuses on whether the product satisfies the user's needs — 'fitness for use'. Crosby defined quality as conformance to requirements; Taguchi introduced the 'loss to society' concept.

questions.text: A hospital drug that works perfectly but has packaging that makes patients doubt its effectiveness is a failure in which Garvin dimension?
questions.explanation: Perceived Quality is about what customers believe based on indirect cues (brand, appearance, reputation) — not actual performance. The drug performs well but is perceived poorly.

questions.text: Quality Assurance (QA) is reactive — it finds and fixes defects after they occur.
questions.explanation: QA is proactive — it builds systems and standards to prevent defects. Quality Control (QC) is the reactive activity of detecting and correcting defects.

questions.text: A data pipeline delivers results on schedule and with no missing records, but 8% of values are out of valid range. Which quality dimension is primarily violated?
questions.explanation: Values out of valid range violate the Validity dimension of data quality. Completeness (missing records) and Timeliness (on schedule) are both fine here.

questions.text: ISO 9001 is a Quality Assurance standard focused on building systems that prevent defects.
questions.explanation: ISO 9001 is an internationally recognised QA standard that specifies requirements for a quality management system — it is process-focused and preventive, not just inspection-based.
